en: The titles of the teachings of the *Garbhadhātu-vajra* were compiled by the śramaṇa Aratandrita (translated into Chinese as Yicao) of the East Pagoda Cloister at Qinglong Monastery;
[this includes] the title of Tathāgata Mahāvairocana as Samantaprabha-vajra.

In the east is the Tathāgata Ratnaketu, named Puṇyaskandhavajra; in the south is the Tathāgata Saṃkusumitarāja, titled Samatāvajra; in the west is the Tathāgata Amitāyus, titled Viśuddhavajra; in the north is the Tathāgata Dundubhisvara, titled Akṣobhyavajra; in the southeast is the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, the Tathatāvajra; in the northeast is the Bodhisattva Maitreya, titled Vegavajra; in the southwest is the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, titled Śrīvajra; in the northwest is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, titled Dharmavajra; and in the center is the Bodhisattva Prajñāpāramitā, the Jñānavajra.

To the right is the Great Majestic Vajra Temple of Yamāntaka, the Radiant Vajra; to the right is the Most Victorious Vajra of Trailokyavijaya Bodhisattva; and to the right is the Swift Vajra of Hayagrīva, the Illuminating King, also known as the Devouring Vajra.
To the left is the noble Trailokyavijaya Bodhisattva, Hūṃkāravajra; to the left is Acala Bodhisattva, Nityavajra; to the left is Candogra Bodhisattva, Tilavajra.
In the center is the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha with the Cintāmaṇivajra;

to his right is the Bodhisattva Dānapāramitā with the Viśvadānavajra; to her right is the Bodhisattva Śīlapāramitā with the Śīlavajra; to her right is the Bodhisattva Kṣāntipāramitā with the Kṣitivajra; to her right is the Bodhisattva Vīryapāramitā with the Maitrīrakṣaṇavajra; and to her right is the Bodhisattva Dhyānapāramitā with the Samyaktvavajra.

On the left side is the Bodhisattva Prajñāpāramitā, Mahājñānavajra; on the left side is the Bodhisattva Upāyapāramitā, Niṣṭhāvajra-Kauśalyavajra; on the left side is the Bodhisattva Praṇidhānapāramitā, Siddhivajra; on the left side is the Bodhisattva Balapāramitā, Vīryaprasthānavajra; and on the left side is the Bodhisattva Jñānapāramitā, Paripūrṇaviśuddhavajra.

To the right is the Bodhisattva Intention-Arousing Turning of the Wheel of Dharma, holding the Vajra of the Wheel of Dharma; to the right is the Bodhisattva Arising of the Foundations of Mindfulness, holding the Vajra of Retentive Memory; to the right is the Noble Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, holding the Hook-Vajra; to the right is the Bodhisattva Amoghapāśa, manifesting as the Transformation-Vajra; and to the right is the Bodhisattva Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara, the Great Compassion-Vajra.

To the left is the Bodhisattva Vimalagati, the Vajra of Clear Pervasion; to the left is the Bodhisattva Subāhu, the Vajra of Siddhi; to the left is the Bodhisattva Vajrasūcī, the Vajra of Diligence; to the left is the Bodhisattva Susiddhikara, the Vajra of Accomplishment; to the left is the Bodhisattva Vajragarbharāja, the Vajra of Secrecy; and to the left is the Bodhisattva Maṇḍala, the Vajra of the Great Wheel.

To the right is the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi with the Vajra of Wish-Fulfilling Jewels; to the right is the Bodhisattva-Mātṛkā Mahāmāyūrī with the Vajra; to the right is the Rākṣasa King Ekajaṭī with the Vajra of Thunder and Lightning; and to the right is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of the Eleven Faces with the Mutated Vajra.

To the left of the first [deity] on the south side of the western gate is the Bodhisattva Amoghasiddhi-vajra, the Vajra of Accomplishing Affairs; to his left is the Bodhisattva Cundā-vajra, the Vajra of Nectar; to his left is the Bodhisattva Vajrasena-vajra, the Vajra of the General; and to his left is the Bodhisattva Vajratārā-vajra, the Vajra of the Vidyādhara.

In the first tier facing north, from the second position on the west: the Bodhisattva Mahābodhi is named Vajra Radiating Light; the third is the Honored Bodhisattva Tārā, Vajra Born of Compassion; the fourth is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, named Dharma-vajra; the fifth is the Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī, Vajra Subduer; the sixth is the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, Vajra Holder of the Wheel; and the seventh is the Bodhisattva Producing the Lotus Family, Vajra of Inexhaustibility.

On the second tier facing north, starting from the first on the west: the Bodhisattva Śāntamati is named Samantaprabhā-vajra; the second, the Bodhisattva Mahāśrīmati, is Nityotsava-vajra; the third, the Bodhisattva Mahāśrīmahāvidyā, is Ratnagarbha-vajra; the fourth, the Bodhisattva Cintāmaṇicakra, is Ratnadharā-vajra; the fifth, the Bodhisattva Yaśodharā, is Vidyotana-vajra; the sixth, the Bodhisattva Stūpamahāśrī, is Hitasukha-vajra; and the seventh, the Bodhisattva Mahāpratisarā, is Varadā-vajra.

On the third tier from the north, starting from the first position on the west: White-Clad Bodhisattva (Pāṇḍaravāsini), Vajra Free from Defilement; Second, Great Auspicious Transformation Bodhisattva (Mahāmangalavikurvaṇa), Vajra of Dynamic Activity; Third, Water-Auspiciousness Bodhisattva (Jalaśrī), Vajra of Moistening Birth; Fourth, Amoghapāśa Bodhisattva, Vajra of Equanimity (Samādhi); Fifth, Wealthy Bodhisattva (Vasumdhara), Vajra of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel; Sixth, White-Body Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Vajra of Universal Transformation; Seventh, Parṇaśavarī Bodhisattva, Vajra of Extraordinary Conduct.

On the fourth tier from the north, starting from the first on the west: the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin is Viramāra-vajra; the second, the Bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati, is Atikrānta-vajra; the third, the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, is Adhyātma-bhāvana-vajra, also named Vyaktalakṣaṇa-vajra; the fourth, the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi, is Paripūrṇa-vajra; the fifth, the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, is Karuṇāpraṇidhāna-vajra; the sixth, the Bodhisattva Ratnaprabha, is Śubha-ratna-vajra; the seventh, the Bodhisattva Ratnamudrā, is Mudrādharā-vajra; the eighth, the Bodhisattva Amoghadarśin, is Samantadarśin-vajra; and the ninth, the Bodhisattva Sarvāśāparipūraka, is Mahāmokṣa-vajra.

On the first tier facing south, starting from the second position on the west: the Bodhisattva Vajramuṣṭi is the Secret Vajra; the third is the Bodhisattva Vajrakoṭidhara, the Swift Vajra; the fourth is the Bodhisattva Vajrasattva, the Suchness Vajra; the fifth is the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Firm Vajra; the sixth is the Bodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśa, the Summoning Vajra; and the seventh is the Bodhisattva Vajrakulodbhava, the Indestructible Vajra.

On the second tier facing south, starting from the first position on the west: the Bodhisattva Vimalakīrti (Free from Discursive Elaboration) with the Vajra of Non-differentiated Speech; second, the Bodhisattva Vajradhara with the Vajra of Constant Stability; third, the Bodhisattva Vajrasphoṭa with the Vajra of Firm Adherence; fourth, the Bodhisattva Gaganānantavyūha with the Vajra of Vastness and the Vajra of Transcendence; fifth, the Bodhisattva Krodhavajradhara with the Vajra of Majestic Power; sixth, the Bodhisattva Vajrasudṛḍha with the Vajra of Protection; and seventh, the Bodhisattva Gaganāmala with the Vajra of Freedom from Defilement.

On the third tier facing south, starting from the first position on the west: the Bodhisattva Vajratīkṣṇa holds the Prajñā-vajra; the second, the Bodhisattva Vajrasūkṣma, holds the Sūkṣma-vajra; the third, the Bodhisattva Niṣprapañca, holds the Caryā-vajra; the fourth, the Bodhisattva Vajradaṃṣṭra, holds the Damanavajra; the fifth, the Bodhisattva Vajrarati, holds the Ānandavajra; the sixth, the Bodhisattva Vajratīkṣṇa, holds the Kṣurapra-vajra; and the seventh, the Bodhisattva Vajracakra, holds the Vinayavajra.

On the fourth tier facing south, starting from the first on the west: first is the Bodhisattva Sunlight, Vajra of Majestic Virtue; second is the Bodhisattva Dispelling All Heat and Affliction, Vajra Free from Fear; third is the Bodhisattva Compassion-Arising, Vajra of Compassionate Mindfulness; fourth is the Bodhisattva Pitying, Vajra of Rescue and Protection; fifth is the Bodhisattva Inconceivable Wisdom, Vajra Difficult to Measure; sixth is the Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla, Vajra of Skillful Salvation; seventh is the Bodhisattva Bestowing Fearlessness, Vajra of Sovereignty; eighth is the Bodhisattva Destroying Evil Destinies, Vajra of Removing Obstructions; ninth is the Bodhisattva Pitying, Vajra of Rescue and Protection.

At the first tier of the eastern gate is the Vajra that Generates the Wisdom-Seals of All Tathāgatas; proceeding north from the gate, the first is the Supreme Vajra of the Buddha-Eye Mother (Buddhalocanā), and the second is the Most Victorious Vajra of the Seven-Crore Buddhas Mother.
In the south gate, the first is the Bodhisattva Vīravīrya with the seal of Vajra-śīghra; the second is the Bodhisattva Mahāsukhāmogha with the seal of Tattva-vajra.
On the second tier above, facing the door, is Śākyamuni Buddha with the seal of Śānti-vajra.

The attendant Bodhisattva Ākāśa was Anantajvāla-vajra; the attendant Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara was Viśuddha-vajra; the attendant Bodhisattva Aparājita was Jaya-suvrata-vajra; and the attendant Aparājitā was Janma-vajra.

In the northern gate, first is the Vajra of the Jewel-Reality of All Tathāgatas; second, the Vajra of the Sublime Function of the Tathāgata’s Ūrṇā-hair; third, the Vajra of the Great Cakra-vartin Buddha-uṣṇīṣa that Destroys Māras; fourth, the Vajra of the Radiant Mass Buddha-uṣṇīṣa of Supernatural Powers; fifth, the Vajra of the Wondrous Resonance of the Boundless Sound Buddha-uṣṇīṣa; sixth, the Vajra of the Tathāgata’s Compassionate Transformation; seventh, the Vajra of the Tathāgata’s Compassionate Command; and eighth, the Vajra of the Tathāgata’s Compassionate Protection and Mindfulness.

At the southern gate, the first is the White Parasol Uṣṇīṣa, the Vajra of Extraordinary Appearance; the second is the Victorious Uṣṇīṣa, the Great Honored Vajra, also known as the Peerless Vajra; the third is the Most Victorious Uṣṇīṣa, the Greatest Honored Vajra, also known as the Upward-Going Vajra; the fourth is the Lofty Uṣṇīṣa, the Hard-to-Behold Vajra; the fifth is the Shattering Uṣṇīṣa, the Mara-Expelling Vajra; the sixth is the Tathāgata’s Eloquence of Speech Vajra; the seventh is the Tathāgata’s Nature of Speech Emptiness Vajra; and the eighth is the Tathāgata’s Smile of Joy Vajra, also known as the Broken-Face Vajra.

On the fourth tier at the eastern gate, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī is named Prajñāvajra; at the northern side of the gate, first is Jālinīprabha Bodhisattva, Varṇavajra; second is Ratnamakuṭa Bodhisattva, Vyūhavajra; third is Vimalaprabha Bodhisattva, Virajovajra; fourth is Candraprabha Bodhisattva, Tejovajra; and fifth is Pañcacīra Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Śrīvajra.

In the southern gate, first is the Bodhisattva Upakeśinī, Vajra of Sublime Wisdom; second is the Bodhisattva Śāsanadharā, Vajra of Secret Retention; third is the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, Vajra of Auspiciousness; fourth is the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, Vajra of Prajñā; and fifth is the Bodhisattva Ākarṣaṇa, Vajra of Universal Gathering.

To the south of the eastern gate, the first is the Tathāgata-danta Bodhisattva Dharma-protecting Vajra-manifestation Vajra; the second is the Pratyekabuddha Cakrāra Obstacle-crushing Vajra; the third is the Pratyekabuddha Ratnāra Nirvāṇa Vajra; the fourth is the Kauṣṭhila Awakening-nature Vajra, also named Liberation Vajra; the fifth is Ānanda Dharma-collection Vajra; the sixth is Kātyāyana Eloquence Vajra, also named Gushing Spring Vajra; the seventh is Upāli Śīla Vajra; the eighth is Jñānakauṣṭhila Right Cause Vajra, also named Innate Wisdom Vajra; and the ninth is the Offering Ocean-cloud Universal Covering Vajra.

In the northern gate, the first is the Tathāgata Śokti-jana-caryā-vajra; the second is the Pratyekabuddha Candanagandha-śītalavajra; the third is the Pratyekabuddha Tamālagandha-ghana-vajra; the fourth is Mahāmaudgalyāyana-praṇidhāna-vajra; the fifth is Subhūti-nimitta-vajra; the sixth is Kāśyapa-rajas-vigata-vajra; the seventh is Śāriputra-prajñā-vajra, also named Kuśala-jñāna and Kuśala-kauśalya; the eighth is the Tathāgata Priya-saṃkhyāta-dharma-vajra; and the ninth is the Tathāgata Tyāga-saṃjñā-samatā-vajra.
The general name for all the noble ones of the celestial outer Vajra family is Dharmapāla-vajra (Vajra Protector of the Dharma).
The names of the Vajras of the Vajradhātu are:
Vairocana Mahāvairocana, the Unobstructed Universal Illuminator; Akṣobhya Buddha, the Immovable One Free from Fear; and Ratna... [the Jewel].
The great merit of the various practices of the equality of birth and Buddhahood; the pure lifespan of the Great Compassion of Amitāyus Buddha;
the activity and function of the accomplishment of *siddhi* by Amoghasiddhi Buddha; the firmness and solidity of the Vajra-pāramitā;
the Jewel-vajra of the Ratna-pāramitā, also known as the Holder of Jewels; and the Lotus of the Dharma-pāramitā.
Purity; the wondrous activity of the *karma-pāramitā*; the great heroism of the *sattva-bodhisattva-tathatā*;
the sovereign Bodhisattva King holding the hook; the Bodhisattva Love who is free from pleasure and free from craving;
the Bodhisattva Well-Being who praises peace and happiness; the Bodhisattva Jewel, the great wish-fulfilling treasury; and the Bodhisattva Light.
The Bodhisattva Majestic Virtue and Radiance; the Bodhisattva Perfectly Fulfilled Vows; the Bodhisattva Subtle Smile, Joyful and Delighted;
the Bodhisattva Dharma, the Lotus of the True Dharma; the Bodhisattva Benefit, Wisdom that Eliminates Karmic Obstructions;
the Bodhisattva Cause, Non-retrogression from Bodhi; the Bodhisattva Language, Sublime Speech of the Emptiness of Nature; the Bodhisattva Karma, Virtue.
The Bodhisattva Skillful Discernment of Affairs; the Bodhisattva Invincible Protector of Diligence;
the Yakṣa Bodhisattva Dharma-Protector Subduer; the Fist Bodhisattva Secret; the Playful Bodhisattva Universal Reverence Good; the Garland Bodhisattva Wondrous Adornment Vajra;
the Song Bodhisattva Wondrous Sound Vajra, also named Fearless; and the Dance Bodhisattva Wondrous Pervasion Vajra.
The Vajra of Firmness: the Bodhisattva Vajra of Swift Action, the Vajra of Majestic Form; the Bodhisattva of Flower-Sprinkling:
the Vajra of Wondrous Color, the Vajra of Purity; the Bodhisattva of Lamps: the Vajra of Universal Illumination, the Vajra that Dispels Darkness;
the Bodhisattva of Incense-Ointment: the Vajra of Cool Refreshment, the Vajra of Supreme Purity; the Bodhisattva of the Hook: the Summoner.
The Bodhisattva Saṃcayavajrā, the Bodhisattva Pāśavajrā, the Bodhisattva Sparśavajrā, the Bodhisattva Maitrīvajrā, the Bodhisattva Muditāvajrā,
the Bodhisattva Śṛṅkhalāvajrā, the Bodhisattva Sthiravajrā, and the Bodhisattva Ghaṇṭāvajrā are the Vajras of Liberation.
Next are the sixteen bodhisattvas of the Bhadrakalpa:
Maitreya, Śīghravajra, Amoghadarśin, Samantadarśivajra,
Apāyamjaha, Sarvatrāṇavajra, Aśokāntaravimuktivajra, Gandhavyūhamahābalavajra, and Parākrama.
Avinivartanīya-vajra, Gaganagañja-śrī, Jñānaketu-jñānapūrṇa-dharmapūrṇa-vajra,
Bhadrapāla-sukhapāla-vajra, Amitaprabha-mahāvidyā-vajra, Jālinīprabha-upāya, Candraprabha-śītalā-vajra,
Akṣayamati-pratibhānasaṃcaya-vajra, and Akṣayamati-bhūtārtha-ratna.
Vajragarbha is the Vajra who upholds the Teaching and is also called the Vajra who Establishes Verification;
Samantabhadra is the Vajra of Universal Gathering; the Bodhisattva Dāna is the Vajra of Universal Bestowal; the Bodhisattva Śīla is the Vajra of Pure Precepts;
the Bodhisattva Kṣānti is the Vajra of Imperial Sovereignty; the Bodhisattva Vīrya is the Vajra of Compassionate Protection; the Bodhisattva Dhyāna is the Vajra of Correct...
Adi-vajra, the Wisdom Bodhisattva Mahā-prajñā-vajra; Prajñā-pāramitā-vajra, the Expedient Means Bodhisattva Upāya-kauśalya-vajra;
Anuttara-vajra, the Vow Bodhisattva Siddhi-vajra; Bala-vajra, the Bodhisattva of Valiant Progress;
Jñāna-vajra, the Bodhisattva of Perfect Purity; Acala, the Unshakeable Honored One, the Immovable Vajra.
Vajra, the Ever-Abiding Vajra; Trailokyavijaya, the Supreme Vajra; Ṣaḍbhuja, the Vajra of Great Majestic Power;
Hayagrīva, the Vajra of Daring Consumption and Swift Action; Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa, the Nectar;
and Agniśikhin, the Vajra of Great Strength—these twenty divine sages are collectively named the Outer Vajra Family, known as the Protectors.
*Dharmavajra*, also known as *Samantavajra*.
The above is verified against the edition from Qinglong Monastery.
The original record states:
Copied on the twenty-third day of the third month in the second year of Jōei at the quiet window of Gokuraku-bō, based on the manuscript of the late Master.
Completed with one proofreading, etc.
Copied on the fifteenth day of the second month in the second year of Bunkyū at Kankin-in, based on the manuscript of Hōon-in.
Copied on the fifteenth day of the fifth month of the second year of Jōei by Kongo Busshi Genkei at Mokuhata, using the original manuscript from the Sōjū Go-bō.
The *Kongōshi* (Vajra-aid) records that Zen Master Jō’s elegant instruction states: "Those who seek the formless advance, yet cannot emerge; this book is a secret treasury," and so forth. Above.
